skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

version.changelog: v1.1.6: 修复元数据声明 - 在SKILL.md头部yaml metadata中显式声明required_env，解决Registry metadata declares no required env vars 问题

llm.summary: The scripts and instructions match the stated purpose (scan OpenClaw session files, extract memories with the agent, and write results to Feishu), but the skill will read local conversation files and transmit extracted content to Feishu — make sure you trust that data flow and provide your own Feishu credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description, SKILL.md, and scripts consistently implement automated extraction from OpenClaw session files and writing to Feishu (L2/L3/L4). Required tools (openclaw, python3, bash) and Feishu credentials in SKILL.md and skill.json are appropriate for this purpose. One inconsistency: the registry summary at the top of the submission lists "Required env vars: none," while SKILL.md and skill.json declare several required Feishu environment variables (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID). That mismatch is likely an authoring/metadata error and should be corrected before installation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and the two scripts explicitly read OpenClaw session files (full contents), filter/parse them, invoke the local openclaw agent to perform extraction, and rely on the agent / openclaw CLI to write results to Feishu and send notifications. All of those actions are consistent with the declared purpose. Note: reading full session files and sending their (extracted) content to Feishu is exactly what the skill is designed to do — this is normal for the stated function but does constitute data exfiltration of conversation content to a cloud service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only skill). The package contains two bash scripts that the user is instructed to copy into their workspace; nothing is downloaded from external URLs. This is low install risk, but the scripts will be written into the user's workspace and run by cron or manually.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The environment variables required by the scripts (Feishu open_id, app token, table and doc IDs) are reasonable and necessary for writing to Feishu. However, the registry metadata shown earlier incorrectly stated no required env vars; the actual code and skill.json do require sensitive Feishu credentials (L2_APP_TOKEN etc.). The skill does not request unrelated credentials. Users should supply their own Feishu tokens (not the author's sample values) and ensure those tokens have least privilege necessary for table/document writes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (default) — the skill does not request forced or permanent inclusion. The scripts create files under /root/.openclaw/workspace and /tmp, use a lock under /tmp, and mark processed sessions in workspace memory files; these are normal for this type of utility and do not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:
- Data exposure: this skill will read complete OpenClaw session files and (via the agent/openclaw CLI) write extracted content to Feishu cloud services. Do NOT install it if your sessions contain highly sensitive or regulated data unless you accept that transmission and storage in Feishu is allowed.
- Credentials: provide your own FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID in the workspace .env. Do NOT use the author's example IDs. Create Feishu app credentials with the minimum permissions needed and be prepared to rotate them if compromised.
- Registry metadata mismatch: the public registry entry incorrectly listed no required env vars. Confirm required env vars are present before running and ask the publisher to correct the registry metadata.
- Test first in a safe environment: run the scripts on a sample/non-sensitive session directory to verify behavior and outputs. Check what the agent writes to your Feishu resources.
- OpenClaw / CLI dependency: the scripts call openclaw agent and openclaw message send; ensure openclaw is installed, authenticated, and that the openclaw CLI commands behave as expected on your system.
- Cron and permissions: the installation instructions place scripts under /root/.openclaw/workspace and expect crontab usage; run under the intended user account and review file ownership. Avoid running as root unnecessarily.
- Audit and review: inspect the scripts yourself (they are included) and optionally run them with verbose logging (remove redirection to /dev/null) to see error messages and outputs. If you have strict security requirements, consider running in an isolated environment or disabling automatic cron triggers until you are satisfied.
- If anything is unclear (e.g., unexpected network endpoints, extra env vars), request clarification from the author before use.
